title: Signal Corral: Error Cluster Triage Stream for Console Debugging
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Design a compact, stream-first UI component for the Redwood Console called 'Signal Corral' that surfaces grouped error clusters (by taxonomy and request signature), their retry behavior, and quick payload inspection. This component must fit into the existing Request Insights and Dashboards flows and offer lightweight interactions for operators to: collapse/expand clusters, surface root-cause signals, pivot between retry attempts, and open a full payload inspector. The prototype should validate layout patterns for high-density lists, affordances for canary/rollout attribution, and cost context per cluster (tokens and estimated cost).
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows clustered view with at least three clustering dimensions (error-class, endpoint signature, and retry-origin)
Each cluster row exposes: count, representative error snippet, last-seen timestamp, retry-rate indicator, and estimated token-cost metric
Clicking a cluster expands an inline mini-timeline showing up to 5 recent attempts and a quick 'open payload inspector' action
Design includes mobile/compact variant for narrow console panes and an accessible color palette that maps to error taxonomy
Handoff artifacts (Figma frames + annotated specs) delivered with tokens/cost guidance and component accessibility notes
tasks: Build low-fidelity flows exploring list density and inline timeline (Sofia)
Design high-fidelity Figma frames including compact and expanded states (Aanya)
Run 3 moderated usability sessions with Support and SRE to validate discovery affordances (Sofia + PM)
Consolidate feedback and produce final handoff doc with CSS vars, spacing, and tokens (Aanya)
Coordinate with ENG for feasibility call around inline KV cache preview and cost calculation (design sync)
Create a short spec for rollout attribution badges (canary/dedicated/private)
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Chose clustered-first approach vs. single-request timeline to improve triage throughput for SRE teams
2025-02-13: Use three clustering keys (error taxonomy, request signature hash, retry-origin) to balance specificity and signal prevalence
2025-02-14: Inline mini-timeline chosen over modal for majority quick-inspect flows to reduce context switching
2025-02-15: Show estimated token-cost at cluster level (rounded) — product approved to expose cost with low-fidelity accuracy and a tooltip explaining estimation methodology
review_feedback: PM (Marco Li) 2025-02-16: Prefer stronger visual separation between retry-origin types (region vs. capacity vs. model-variant)
Eng (Rae Thompson) 2025-02-16: Inline payload preview must be limited to 1KB and sanitized — engineering will add server-side truncation
SRE (Jordan Kim) 2025-02-17: Add a filter for 'only regressions' using evaluation baselines — good to expose as label
Design leadership (Maya Ortiz) 2025-02-17: Reduce micro-animations for very dense lists to keep CPU cost low on customer consoles
usability_findings: Session 1: Ops users preferred a single-click expand on cluster row, not a small chevron icon
Session 2: Participants confused by 'estimated cost' units — we added a tooltip and currency/token toggle
Session 3: Support team valued ability to pin a cluster to an incident and share a deep link
next_steps: Incorporate engineering constraints from feasibility call (expected 2025-02-20)
Finalize accessible color tokens and produce CSS variables
Prepare implementation grooming ticket with ENG and attach Figma frames
Add acceptance test scenarios for token-cost accuracy in QA checklist
